fatal_errors: The proposed intervention is an undefined placeholder rather than a specified thermal-aging treatment.
The material is incorrectly treated as a single-phase solid solution; the target is an as-cast FCC+B2 eutectic AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy.
No aging temperatures, durations, or loading conditions are defined.
The proposed grain-size/dislocation-density/grain-boundary-cohesion mechanism does not match the L12 ordering, jagged FCC/B2 phase-boundary, planar-slip, and plastic-instability mechanism.
The prediction omits the non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile transition and the contrasting behavior near 600 and 750 degrees Celsius.
No prior observations or evidence are supplied.
The falsification experiment is an undefined placeholder and cannot discriminate the hypothesis.
explanation: The response only echoes the broad themes of thermal exposure, loading, and improved toughness. It does not reconstruct a concrete intervention or testable hypothesis. It misses the dual-phase initial structure, the 550–750 degrees Celsius transition window, maximal L12 ordering and jagged phase boundaries near 600 degrees Celsius, ductility recovery near 750 degrees Celsius, and the required microscopy evidence of pile-ups and crack initiation at phase-boundary tips without impurity segregation. Although comparison with the same untreated alloy is conceptually appropriate, the absent conditions, evidence, and measurable falsification criterion make the hypothesis unsupported.
